_source: docs/tech-plan/Content-Reveal.md §5.2–5.3 (story_mw56vk3i_8). Placeholder lines until Dialog-Unification F5 moves the Collective's hub lines into the dialog doc §10; the captains speak their own voice-pack lines.

collective.newPlanet: {planet} is on the ledger. Same terms as before: we buy the common and the uncommon you lift, up to the quota, and everything past it is yours. Maps one to three are posted.

outpost._source: Outpost-Design §2.2 (draft lines; the owner's own words kept) [MM-story_mw5oe8km_k]. One set per planet. The other eight (air … greenies) are O11 DRAFTS FOR OWNER REVIEW [MM-story_mw5oeob4_s], written in each captain's voice (missions.json capitalShips; voicepacks.json characters and phrases) to the same four beats and the same facts: the contract grants only the base, the player builds power, a mining station on the planet's common ore and a storage tower with their own gold, and raids will come.

ground.line: You have done well gathering what lies on the surface of Verdance. Better than most of my own regiments.
So tell me: how are you at mining? And farming?
We have a site for you: an outpost base on the mesa. Build your power, a mining station on the iron and a storage tower with your own gold, and the place is yours to run.
Not everybody aboard is happy about your progress. Help us bring up the ore and you will earn some moral equity with the realm. There will be opposition. We will pay well.

air.line: You picked Florael's meadows clean and still came home in one piece, little one. Half my squadron could learn from that.
So tell me: ever had your hands in the ground instead of the sky? Mining, I mean.

There's an outpost base on the mesa down there, and it's yours. That's all I'm handing you. Build your power, a mining station on the magnesium and a storage tower with your own gold, and you run the place.

Not every pilot aboard likes how fast you're climbing, and some of them will come at that mesa. Keep your guns up and bring the magnesium home. The Dawnwing pays well, and the dawn keeps its promises.

hightech.line: Your surface yields on Ochre beat our forecasts. I checked the numbers twice; they hold.
Next question, then: can you run extraction? Not salvage. Mining.
We have a site: an outpost base on the mesa, and nothing more. Build your power, a mining station on the silicon and a storage tower with your own gold. Run it well and the outpost is yours.
Not everyone on the Meridian likes a contractor outperforming the division, and some of them will come at that mesa. Expect it. Bring up the silicon and we will pay well. I sign my name to that.

artillery.line: You worked Kessra's craters cleaner than my own survey crews. Good ranging.
Now tell me: can you dig as well as you gather?
There is an outpost base on the mesa, ranged and cleared. That is all we hand you. Build your power, a mining station on the nickel and a storage tower with your own gold, and the site is yours.

Some of the gun crews aboard do not like your progress, and they will not stay at their posts over it. Expect them on that mesa. Bring the nickel up and Siegeholm pays well. I answer for each round, and I will answer for this.

water.line: You gathered from Rime's ice like one of the Reef-Born, landwalker. The shoal noticed.
But can you go deeper than the surface? Can you mine?

There is a mesa above the frozen ponds with an outpost base on it, and that base is yours. Build your power, a mining station on the manganese and a storage tower with your own gold, and the place is yours to keep.
Not every clan aboard is glad of you. Some will come for that mesa the way raiders come for the shoal. Bring up the manganese and the Reef-Born will pay well. The reef remembers who guards it.

arcane.line: You gathered from Cinder's ash fields and harmed no one doing it. The faithful noticed.
Tell me, then: will you work the deep places too? Will you mine?

There is an outpost base on the mesa above the lava pools. That is all the Cathedral gives. Build your power, a mining station on the zinc and a storage tower with your own gold, and it is yours to tend.
Some aboard say the Hierophant's ore should never pass through an outsider's hands, and they will come to that mesa. Bring up the zinc for the people, not the throne, and we will pay well.

space.line: Your survey of Lumen's surface matched our charts better than our own teams managed.
So, next on my list: how are you at mining?

We've charted a site for you: an outpost base on the mesa between the craters. Build your power, a mining station on the thorium and a storage tower with your own gold, and the outpost is yours. By the charter.
Not everyone in the fleet likes a local moving this fast, and some of them will come for that mesa. My protection doesn't reach the surface. Bring up the thorium and the fleet pays well.

dark.line: You gathered among the glowing groves of Xenthe and left them whole. The Movement saw that.
Would you go beneath them? Would you mine for us?
There is an outpost base on the mesa, and I can give you that much. Build your power, a mining station on the neodymium and a storage tower with your own gold, and it is yours.
Not every sister aboard wants an unawakened outsider holding our ground. Some will come to that mesa, and I cannot stop them all. Bring up the neodymium and we will pay well. I'll answer for it.

greenies.line: You gathered from Vexmire's bogs and took no more than you needed. The hive marked it, single stalk.
Now: will you tend the deep stores as well? Can you mine?
There is an outpost base on the mesa between the hive mounds, held in trust for you. Build your power, a mining station on the sulfur and a storage tower with your own gold, and it is yours to tend.
Not every part of the hive wants a single stalk keeping its own stores. Some will come to that mesa. Bring up the sulfur for the whole, and the Ark will pay well.

farm._source: Farming-Design §2.2 [MM-story_mwcuzyf7_3k]. The farming contract is offered in person by the planet faction's Factor, its Neutral (N) character, at the Trade Station (src/farm/factor.js). DRAFT LINES FOR OWNER REVIEW, written in the Factor's own voice (voicepacks.json phrases and motivation). One set per planet (all nine drafted 2026-11-23 [MM-story_mwu3uc19_1v]; the game plays Verdance F1, so the other eight wait for their F1 to go live). gate: farming is shut (the planet is not finished yet: every campaign map beaten, owner 2026-11-12), so the Factor says what it waits on. offer: F1 is on offer, then the contract card. accept / later: the reply to the card. farm: the contract is the player's.

gate.line: Quartermaster's desk. Everything that comes aboard Halbrecht's Oath goes through my ledger, and everything that goes down to Verdance comes out of it.
Land to farm? The regiments eat, so I'm listening. But nobody ploughs a field the enemy still walks across.
Finish the fight for Verdance, every last map of it, and come see me. I'll have the paperwork ready.

offer.line: Your rig made Mk II. I watched the tonnage come through; the numbers hold.
So here's a line item for you. The regiments need bread, and your outpost leaves free ground at the mesa's foot.
I'll sign over a Farmhouse and a crate of Loam Grain seed. Plant it, bring the harvest aboard, and the ledger pays. Do we have a deal?

accept.line: Noted. Filed. The Farmhouse is on its way down. Don't make me write it off.

later.line: Suit yourself. It stays in the ledger until you want it. Flags don't balance the books, and neither does an empty field.

farm.line: The Farmhouse is on the books. Bring the Loam Grain aboard when it's in; I count every sack.

gate.line: Trade Station, Dawnwing Carrier. I fix wings mostly. Lately I fix the seed ledger too.
You want to grow silk down there? Sky's a machine. It doesn't care what you plant, but the raiders do.
Finish Florael, every map of it, then come back. I'll have the crate ready. Logged it.

offer.line: Florael's quiet. Quiet enough for flowers, anyway.
The pilots need parachute silk and I'm tired of buying it off-planet. Petal Silk grows in rows beside your outpost.
Farmhouse, a crate of Petal Silk seed, and an oxygen tank rig when you're done. Just tell me what's bent if it goes wrong. Deal?

accept.line: Logged it. Farmhouse goes down on the next lift. Don't crash it.

later.line: Fine. The crate's not going anywhere. Neither am I.

farm.line: Bring the silk up when it's in. I'll check the weave myself.

gate.line: Devlin Cho, actuarial. Every crate aboard Sterling Meridian has a price, and I set it.
A farm on Ochre? The base rate for crops on a contested planet is zero. Not low. Zero.
Finish Ochre, every map. Then the risk drops enough to price. Come see me.

offer.line: Ochre's settled. I've rerun the tables; the variance is acceptable.
Sunsalt grows in flooded pans, and the labs burn through it. Your outpost has the ground.
A Farmhouse, a crate of Sunsalt cores, and amber grow lights when you deliver. The expected value is in your favour. Do you take it?

accept.line: Priced in. The Farmhouse ships down. Don't make me revise the forecast.

later.line: Declining is also a position. The offer stays on my books.

farm.line: Bring the Sunsalt aboard. I weigh every pan against the projection.

gate.line: Logistician Farrell. Shells in, targets out. Lately, rations in too.
You can't farm a range while it's still taking fire. That's the cost, logged.
Finish Kessra, every map. Then we talk about what grows on the mesa.

offer.line: Kessra's quiet. The guns are cooling. Good.
Slag Iron grows in rust beds, and the foundry eats it by the tonne. Your outpost has the flat ground.
A Farmhouse and a crate of Slag Iron cores. Plant it, deliver it, and the ledger pays. The ledger doesn't lie. Agreed?

accept.line: Allocated. The Farmhouse goes down with the next supply drop.

later.line: Understood. The order stays on file until you're ready to fill it.

farm.line: Iron comes up, shells go out. Keep the beds turning.

gate.line: Old Brack. I ferry what Reefmother Leviathan needs and keep no side, landwalker.
Ice farms on Rime? The tide doesn't wait for a war to finish, but the farmer has to.
Finish Rime, every map, and come find me at the station. The fare's the fare.

offer.line: Rime's waters are still now. Still enough to cut ice.
Brine Ice freezes in pans by your outpost, and the ship drinks it. Every tribe drinks it.
A Farmhouse, a crate of Brine Ice cores, and blue grow lights when the first load comes aboard. Will you take the passage?

accept.line: Another passage logged. The Farmhouse rides down with the next boat.

later.line: The current will bring you back. It always does.

farm.line: Bring the ice aboard before it melts on the deck.

gate.line: Archivist Balthus. Every grain that enters the Cathedral of the Lamp is recorded. I keep. I do not judge.
You ask to till Cinder while it still burns with conflict. The entry would read 'premature'.
Complete Cinder, every map. Then return, and we will write the terms.

offer.line: Cinder is quiet. The record shows it.
Ash Basalt grows in the lava beds beside your outpost. The kilns require it.
A Farmhouse, a crate of Ash Basalt cores, and red grow lights on delivery. By the terms as written. Do you accept?

accept.line: Noted and shelved. The Farmhouse descends.

later.line: The terms remain on the shelf. They do not expire.

farm.line: Deliver the basalt. Each load is entered under your name.

gate.line: Navigator Vector. I plot supply courses for Vale's Horizon. Food is a course I have not yet plotted.
Lumen has no air and an active war. Projected yield of a farm under those conditions: nil.
Complete Lumen, all maps. Recalculating when you return.

offer.line: Lumen secured. Outcome within tolerance.
No air on the surface, so the trays are sealed. A Vertical farm stands by your outpost; Regolith grows inside.
A Farmhouse, a sealed Vertical farm, a crate of Regolith cores, and pressurised air tanks on delivery. Course plotted. Confirm?

accept.line: Confirmed. Farmhouse and trays inbound. Course plotted.

later.line: Holding pattern. The offer remains on the plot.

farm.line: Deliver the Regolith. I will log each load against the forecast.

gate.line: Doctrinist Vera. I edit the manifesto. Supply aboard The Manifesto is one of its clauses.
A garden in the dark before the dark is settled? That's a revision, not a crusade, and it isn't due yet.
Finish Xenthe, every map. Then the clause can be drafted. Noted.

offer.line: Xenthe is quiet. The draft can proceed.
Glowcap Spores grow in the shade by your outpost. The crew reads by their light.
A Farmhouse, a crate of Glowcap spores, and violet grow lights on delivery. Per the manifesto, this is a fair clause. Do you sign?

accept.line: Signed. Filed. The Farmhouse goes down tonight.

later.line: Unsigned, then. The draft stays open.

farm.line: Bring the spores aboard. Count them in the dark; they glow.

gate.line: Composter Null-7. Intake station, Hivemother Ark. All grades return.
Cultivation on Vexmire is scheduled after the conflict decomposes. Not before.
Finish Vexmire, every map. Then report for intake.

offer.line: Vexmire conflict: decomposed. Soil: ready.
Mire Peat grows in the bog beds beside your outpost. The hive requires it. Yield noted.
A Farmhouse, a crate of Mire Peat, and fertilizer on delivery. This is not a request; it is a schedule. Do you accept the schedule?

later.line: Deferred. The offer sits in the mulch. It will keep.

farm.line: Deliver the peat. Logged for decomposition. That is a compliment.
